candidates.statement: Consider a 3-component link $L=\{L_1, L_2, L_3\}$ in $S^3$ parametrized by $\{\mathsf{x}(s),\mathsf{y}(t),\mathsf{z}(u)\}$ and the following map $$\begin{gathered} \label{eq:F} F_L:S^1\times S^1\times S^1\stackrel{L}{\longrightarrow} \text{Conf}(S^3,3)\stackrel{H}{\longrightarrow} S^2,\qquad L(s,t,u)=(\mathsf{x}(s), \mathsf{y}(t), \mathsf{z}(u))\ . \end{gathered}$$ In order to explain the map $H:\text{Conf}(S^3,3)\longrightarrow S^2$, one must notice that $\text{Conf}(S^3,3)\subset S^3\times S^3\times S^3$ is diffeomorphic to $S^3\times \text{Conf}(\mbox{\bbb R}^3,2)=S^3\times \mbox{\bbb R}^3\times (\mbox{\bbb R}^3\setminus\{0\})$, and consequently deformation retracts onto $S^3\times S^2$.

candidates.section_title: Definition of ``123-helicity'' on invariant unlinked handlebodies.

candidates.statement: Before we start we must point out the following identity (valid for any 3-form $\gamma$ on $M\times M\times M$ and vector fields $X_1,X_2,X_3$ on $M$) $$(\iota_{X_1}\iota_{X_2}\iota_{X_3}\gamma)\wedge\mu\wedge\mu\wedge\mu= \gamma(X_1,X_2,X_3)\,\mu\wedge\mu\wedge\mu=\gamma\wedge\iota_{X_1}\mu\wedge\iota_{X_2}\mu\wedge\iota_{X_3}\mu\ .$$ The first equation follows from the definition, the second equation is a consequence of the fact that $\iota_X$ is an antiderivation i.e. $$\label{eq:iota-antiderivation} \iota_X(\alpha\wedge\beta)=(\iota_X\alpha)\wedge\beta+(-1)^{|\alpha|}\alpha\wedge(\iota_X\beta),$$ and $\iota_{X_i}\mu_j\equiv 0$ for $i\neq j$.

For the proof of $(ii)$ we must show the following $$\int_\mathcal{T} m_{X_1,X_2,X_3}\,\mu_1\wedge \mu_2\wedge \mu_3=\int_{g(\mathcal{T})} m_{g_\ast X_1,g_\ast X_2, g_\ast X_3}\,\mu_1\wedge \mu_2\wedge \mu_3\ .$$ Theorem [\[th:multi-ergodic\]](#th:multi-ergodic){reference-type="ref" reference="th:multi-ergodic"}, tells us that $m_{X_1,X_2,X_3}$ and $m_{g_\ast X_1,g_\ast X_2, g_\ast X_3}$ admit $L^1$-averages $\bar{m}_{X_1,X_2,X_3}$ and $\bar{m}_{g_\ast X_1,g_\ast X_2, g_\ast X_3}$, under actions of $X_i$ and $g_\ast X_i$ respectively.
Clearly, for $\mathsf{H}_{123}(X;\mathcal{T})$ to be nontrivial $\mathcal{T}$ must be of nonzero measure.
This clearly must be the case as we deal with the same topological invariants of links via a different approach.
These approaches should be equivalent to the one presented here in the sense that invariants obtained this way measure the same topological information.
